How to Decide Where a Phrase Attaches
 Ask: Which word is this phrase modifying?
 If the phrase describes the event or action, it usually attaches to 
the verb. 
 If the phrase describes an entity, it usually attaches to the noun. 
 Parsing is therefore closely tied to semantic interpretation.

Attachment Ambiguity
 A major challenge in parsing is attachment ambiguity. 
 Example: 
 The teacher discussed the essay with the student.
 Interpretation A: 
 with the student modifies discussed
 meaning: the teacher talked to the student
 Interpretation B: 
 with the student modifies essay
 meaning: the essay is about / associated with the student
 Different meanings require different parses.

What Is Syntactic Parsing?
 POS tags tell us the category of each word. 
 Parsing tells us how the words are structurally related. 
 Parsing helps answer questions such as: 
 Which noun is the subject? 
 Which phrase is the object? 
 What does a prepositional phrase modify? 
 Two major views of syntax are: 
 dependency structure
 phrase structure

Reading a Dependency Analysis
 To read a dependency 
parse, ask: 
 What is the root? 
 Which words depend 
directly on the root? 
 Which words modify 
nouns? 
 Which phrases modify 
the event? 
 This helps us identify the 
main structure of the 
sentence.

student_query: In Cohen's Kappa, what is expected (chance) agreement and how is it computed from each annotator's label distribution?
gold_context:
Expected Agreement: 𝑃 𝑒
● Expected agreement estimates how much agreement would happen 
by chance. 
● Suppose: 
○ Annotator A assigns Positive to 6/10 items and Negative to 4/10 
○ Annotator B assigns Positive to 5/10 items and Negative to 5/10 
● Then: 
○ chance agreement on Positive = 0.6 × 0.5 = 0.30
○ chance agreement on Negative = 0.4 × 0.5 = 0.20
● So: 
○ 𝑃 𝑒 = 0.30 + 0.20 = 0.50

gold_pages.content:
Expected Agreement: 𝑃 𝑒
● Expected agreement estimates how much agreement would happen 
by chance. 
● Suppose: 
○ Annotator A assigns Positive to 6/10 items and Negative to 4/10 
○ Annotator B assigns Positive to 5/10 items and Negative to 5/10 
● Then: 
○ chance agreement on Positive = 0.6 × 0.5 = 0.30
○ chance agreement on Negative = 0.4 × 0.5 = 0.20
● So: 
○ 𝑃 𝑒 = 0.30 + 0.20 = 0.50

Cohen’s Kappa
● Cohen’s Kappa corrects observed agreement for chance agreement. 
● Formula: 
○ 𝐾 =
𝑃 𝑎 −𝑃 𝑒
1−𝑃 𝑒
● Using the previous example: 
○ 𝑃 𝑎 = 0.70
○ 𝑃 𝑒 = 0.50
○ 𝐾 = 0.70 − 0.50 / 1 − 0.50 = 0.40
● Kappa is more informative than raw agreement alone.

Observed Agreement: 𝑃 𝑎
● Observed agreement is the proportion of cases on which annotators 
agree. 
● Example: 
○ two annotators label 10 items 
○ they agree on 7 items 
● Then: 
○ 𝑃 𝑎 = 7/10 = 0.70
● Observed agreement does not correct for chance agreement.

Module 4 Evaluation Method
o Why evaluation is essential in NLP 
o Benchmark datasets and gold-standard annotations
o Why annotation reliability matters 
o Inter-annotator agreement
o Observed agreement, expected agreement, and Cohen’s Kappa
o The confusion matrix: TP , FP, FN, TN 
o Precision, recall, and F1-score
o When accuracy can be misleading 
o Micro, macro, and weighted averages 
o Entity-level evaluation for NER

Inter-Annotator Agreement
● Human annotations are not always identical. 
● Different annotators may interpret a guideline differently. 
● Inter-annotator agreement measures how consistently humans label 
the same data. 
● High agreement suggests the task and the guidelines are clearer and 
more reliable.

 The task is to assign one POS tag to each token in a sentence.

The BIO Tagging Scheme
● B-X: beginning of an entity of type X

● O: outside any entity

student_query: What is perplexity in language modelling, what does it measure, and does a higher or lower value indicate a better model?
gold_context:
Cross-Entropy Loss
 For each token:
– yi= one-hot true token
– pi= predicted probability
 This penalises: Assigning low probability to correct token
 Intuition: Reward correct next-token predictions.

gold_pages.content:
Cross-Entropy Loss
 For each token:
– yi= one-hot true token
– pi= predicted probability
 This penalises: Assigning low probability to correct token
 Intuition: Reward correct next-token predictions.

Autoregressive Objective
 Autoregressive training objective:
 At each step:
– See previous tokens (i.e. generation history)
– Predict next token
– Compute cross-entropy loss 
– Backpropagate gradients
 The model learns by minimising: Cross-entropy between 
predicted and true tokens.

Language Modelling as Probability Estimation
 Goal of pretraining: Learn the probability distribution over text.
 Formally: 
 Key idea: Model learns to predict each token given previous tokens.

What Is Pretraining?
 Pretraining:
– Large-scale self-supervised training
– Uses raw text (no human labels)
– Learns general language modelling capability
 Goal: Learn to model the probability of text.

Limitation of the Objective
 Since objective is purely predictive, the model may:
– Hallucinate plausible but false information
– Repeat biases in data
– Generate unsafe content
 Fundamentally, it optimises the likelihood of text, not 
correctness or other properties.

socratic_gold_standard: Point the student toward understanding perplexity as a measure of surprise based on token probabilities and the interpretation of high vs low values.
